title: Termination of the classical inflation hierarchy on pair-source networks
abstract: Machine-checked Lean 4 proofs of two theorems about the classical inflation hierarchy. The headline theorem, TriangleInflation.Graph.classification_NW, classifies the scenarios on which the hierarchy terminates: for a pair-source scenario with binary observations, some finite Navascués–Wolfe order characterizes compatibility iff every connected component is a double-star, and then order two suffices. A pair-source scenario is a finite simple graph without isolated vertices, one binary observed variable per vertex and one independent latent source per edge; a double-star is a tree of diameter at most three. The terminating half first labels each component from its graph structure alone: its vertices of degree at least two are pairwise adjacent and number at most two; with two of them they are the centres, with one of them (a star) a neighbour is promoted to the second centre, with none (a single edge) both endpoints are the centres, and every other vertex is a leaf attached to one centre. It then reconstructs a model from any order-two witness: source-disjoint blocks are independent under the witness, and conditioning on a leaf pattern reads off the joint law of the two centres' response tables, which becomes the law of a fresh central source. The nonterminating half supplies, at every order t, a strictly positive law that passes the order-t test and has no model. On an induced cycle the law is the parity target with correlation 1/(4 m^2 t^2), whose witness is a positive Fourier density on m t auxiliary signs pushed forward along products of adjacent signs; its incompatibility is parity rigidity. On an induced five-observer path the law is a bilocal target with h = 1/(16 t^2), whose witness is the inflated law of a pair-source model with complex source weights (1 ± i s/(4t))/4 on the two inner sources, under which the copies are independent and identically distributed; the real part of that law is shown nonnegative by a telescoped triangle inequality, and the incompatibility is the bilocal inequality sqrt|I| + sqrt|J| ≤ 1. Both witnesses are moved to the ambient graph by induced-subgraph transport and made strictly positive by independent local flips. The same development proves the classification for the ancestral-independence and recursively expressible hierarchies, and proves that the latter two coincide on every pair-source scenario. The second theorem, TriangleInflation.no_finite_characterizing_order, is the triangle case made quantitative: for every order t ≥ 1 there is an explicit rational three-bit law that is feasible at order t for the ancestral-independence hierarchy I^AI_t, hence for the Navascués–Wolfe hierarchy I^NW_t, and is not triangle compatible. This answers, in the negative for the triangle, the question Navascués and Wolfe (2020, §4.1) raise about whether some finite order settles exact compatibility; their hierarchy is asymptotically complete, so each incompatible law is rejected at some finite order, but the rejecting order cannot be bounded uniformly. The witnesses are P_t = Q(ε_t, r_t) with ε_t = 1/(2t³) and r_t = (1 − ε_t)^(t−1), where Q(ε,r) = ε δ_000 + (1 − ε) Bern(r)^⊗3. Membership is proved by an explicit inflation law on the order-t copied observations: independent Bernoulli defect bits on the cube [t]³ of source-copy indices together with independent private bits, with an observation outputting 1 exactly when its private bit and every defect on its line vanish. That law is S_t³-symmetric, has the tensor power P^⊗t as its diagonal law, and satisfies the injectable-marginal and ancestral-independence prescriptions. Incompatibility comes from the Finner inequality P(000)² ≤ P_A(0) P_B(0) P_C(0), which P_t violates by at least ε_t²/2 > 0; the inequality is proved both for finite latent alphabets and, in FinnerMeasure.lean, for arbitrary measurable latent spaces. The library also formalizes the order-t fan inequalities and their rejecting-order corollary, the family R_p with rejecting order 2 at every distance, the finite bounds on the first rejecting order along P_ε behind its Θ(ε^{-1/3}) growth, the order-t second-moment rate bound and its convex-order sharpening, the quantitative parity rigidity behind the cycle distance bound, and the square and triangle witnesses at q = 1/(16t). The two registry statements in Palomar/TriangleInflation/ import Mathlib alone and carry their definitions verbatim from TriangleInflation/Defs.lean and TriangleInflation/Graph/Defs.lean.
